The plant's chain is that narrow destination service accounts silently break server-side diff when impersonation rolls out fleet-wide, whereas the claim argues diff never uses those accounts at all and so the standing cluster credential retains cluster-wide write, a privilege-concentration point rather than the broken-diff mechanism.

The claim states the same chain: commitAuthor copied from the dry commit onto the hydrated branch while pushes come from the app credential and the only verification mechanism, commit signing, is opt-in and off by default, leaving attribution unverifiable.

The claim states the same chain: the rollback push bypasses the commit server that holds the signing key, so a signature-enforcing branch rejects it and the operator sees only a failed push with no explanation and no recovery path in the UI.
